test_title: PYST 21 - SSC CHSL 2025 - English Language (Held On: 20 Nov, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: english
question:
Choose the most suitable option to replace the highlighted part of the sentence:

The trend of wearing boots is something that has __**most sure**__ come around this season.
solution:
The correct answer is '4' i.e. most certainly .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase "**most sure**" is incorrect in the sentence because it is grammatically awkward and not a recognized collocation in English.
 
• The correct phrase to use in this context is "**most certainly**" as it aligns with the intended meaning of strong affirmation and suits the sentence structure better.
 
• "Most surely" (Option 1) and "very certainly" (Option 2) are grammatically correct, but they are less natural in this context compared to "most certainly."

Correct sentence: *The trend of wearing boots is something that has **most certainly** come around this season*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Adverbs of Certainty:**
 
 
• Used to express the degree of certainty about an event or action.
 
• Examples include **certainly, surely, undoubtedly, definitely**.
 
• In this context, "most certainly" is the most natural and widely used phrase to express strong affirmation.
